channel.title: SecuBuzz · Cybersecurity News Briefs
channel.description: Fast, factual 60-word cybersecurity briefs and CISA KEV alerts for security professionals.

item.title: Hackers Hijack .GH, .SL, .AS Registries to Issue Rogue TLS Certificates
item.description: Hackers compromised the .GH, .SL, and .AS domain registries, hijacking Google domains and issuing rogue TLS certificates. Security teams can detect these attacks by hunting CT logs and hardening CAA records. The incident exposes registry control weaknesses and threatens domain integrity.

item.title: MonsterCloud CEO Charged for Secret Ransom Payments to Attackers
item.description: The CEO of MonsterCloud, a ransomware remediation firm, faces charges for secretly paying attackers to obtain decryptors while claiming to use proprietary recovery technology. Prosecutors allege the scheme defrauded victims and undermined legitimate recovery efforts, potentially exposing sensitive data and eroding trust in remediation services.

item.title: Cisco Quantum Network Controller Lets Apps Order Entanglement on Demand
item.description: Cisco unveiled a research prototype called the Quantum Network Controller that allows applications to request entanglement from a quantum network. The system delegates delivery coordination to the network, enabling on-demand quantum state distribution without manual hardware setup. The prototype demonstrates a new approach to managing quantum resources.

item.title: Evolution of Web3 in Cloud Supply Chain Attacks
item.description: Unit 42 reports that threat actors are using Web3 infrastructure and open-source supply chain attacks to breach enterprise cloud environments. The attacks exploit vulnerabilities in cloud supply chains, leveraging Web3 tools to gain unauthorized access and compromise cloud resources.

item.title: Australia Considers Mandatory AI Incident Reporting
item.description: Australia is evaluating regulations for AI companies after an agentic attack on its Medicare systems. The government is exploring mandatory incident reporting to better manage AI risks and prevent future disruptions to critical health services.

item.title: FortiBleed Attacks Lock Out FortiGate VPN Administrators
item.description: The FBI reports ongoing FortiBleed attacks targeting exposed Fortinet FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPN gateways, locking out legitimate administrators. The vulnerability allows attackers to gain unauthorized access and disrupt VPN services, prompting urgent patching and network hardening.

item.title: Citizen Lab Criticizes Trump Administration for Pushing Surveillance
item.description: Citizen Lab’s Ron Deibert publicly criticized the Trump administration for promoting widespread surveillance, accusing technology executives of supporting these efforts. The statement highlights concerns over privacy erosion and corporate complicity in government surveillance programs.

item.title: US Offers $10M Reward for Accused Hafnium Hacker
item.description: The United States announced a $10 million reward for information leading to the arrest of Zhang Yu, a key figure in the Hafnium cyber espionage campaign that compromised thousands of computers and exfiltrated large volumes of documents.

item.title: $11 million plan for psychological support at Cyber Command gets fresh boost from lawmakers
item.description: Lawmakers overseeing military cyber policy have added an $11 million mental‑health program to defense spending legislation, ensuring sustained funding for psychological support services at the Cyber Command hub in Fort Meade, Maryland.

item.title: Malicious npm Packages Deliver Overlord RAT and Stealer
item.description: Cybersecurity researchers uncovered a supply‑chain malware campaign that pushed 12 npm packages, eight of which were downloaded 40,767 times. The packages installed the Overlord remote‑access trojan and a credential stealer on compromised hosts, enabling attackers to exfiltrate data and maintain persistence.

item.title: Cloudflare Builds Evidence‑Grounded AI Security Operations
item.description: Cloudflare’s Managed Defense platform deploys AI agents on Workers and global telemetry to separate evidence collection from inference. The system provides grounded, actionable recommendations to analysts, improving the speed and accuracy of security incident response.

item.title: Microsoft FORGE Lab Shares Lessons from AI-Driven Vulnerability Research
item.description: Microsoft Security’s FORGE Lab outlines three key lessons from applying AI to vulnerability research, scaling efforts from Windows to the Linux kernel. The post highlights how machine learning can accelerate discovery, prioritize risks, and improve patching strategies across diverse operating systems.

item.title: Atlassian Patch Addresses CVE-2026-21589 Arbitrary File Access Vulnerability
item.description: Atlassian released patches for multiple products to fix CVE-2026-21589, an arbitrary file access flaw allowing attackers to read any file in the web application’s directory. The vulnerability could expose sensitive configuration files and other confidential data. Users should apply the update immediately to prevent potential data exposure.

item.title: Wiz Red Agent Reveals Public Data Exposure at Fortune 500 Firm
item.description: Wiz’s Red Agent identified a public webpage that exposed sensitive company data within minutes, a flaw missed by traditional DSPM tools. The exposure highlighted gaps in internal‑to‑external scanning and the need for attacker‑thinking security assessments to detect such leaks early.

item.title: Hackers Exploit 32 Zero-Days on Samsung Galaxy S26 at Pwn2Own Ireland
item.description: During the first day of Pwn2Own Ireland 2026, researchers compromised a Samsung Galaxy S26 twice by exploiting 32 zero-day vulnerabilities. The attacks demonstrated the device’s critical weaknesses, allowing full system compromise and data exfiltration, and earned participants $388,500 in prize money.

item.title: Phishing Platform Mimics AI Chatbot Ads to Steal Credentials and MFA Codes
item.description: Cybersecurity researchers uncovered a human-operated phishing platform that impersonates advertising portals for AI chatbots such as ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude. The fake portals lure users into providing credentials and MFA codes, enabling attackers to hijack business accounts and compromise sensitive data.

item.title: Linux Backdoors Disguise Traffic as Email Services to Evade Detection in Korea and Taiwan
item.description: Linux backdoors targeting telecom and network appliances in South Korea and Taiwan disguise their traffic as email services and legitimate processes, using names of real binaries to blend in and avoid detection. The threat actors employ this defense‑evasion technique to maintain persistence on affected systems.

item.title: DNS Root Key Rollover Scheduled for October 11, 2026
item.description: On October 11, 2026, the Internet’s DNS root will switch to a new key‑signing key, KSK‑2024. The change requires resolvers to update trust anchors and verify RFC 8509 trust‑anchor sentinels. Failure to adapt may disrupt name resolution, so operators should test readiness now.

item.title: ‘BigDiskBuster’ Creates Silent Gap in Microsoft Defender Updates
item.description: A proof‑of‑concept technique named BigDiskBuster keeps Microsoft Defender running while blocking its update process, creating a silent detection gap. The method requires no exploit and does not compromise the service itself.

item.title: ASOS Data Breach Confirmed After Hacked Push Notifications
item.description: UK fashion retailer ASOS confirmed a data breach after hackers sent unauthorized push notifications via its mobile app, claiming to have stolen customer data from the company’s Snowflake environment. The breach exposed personal information of customers, prompting ASOS to investigate and notify affected users.

item.title: CISO Perspectives on Managing Vulnerability Risks in the Age of AI
item.description: Microsoft Security Blog discusses how CISOs can mitigate cybersecurity risks and increase resilience using AI-powered vulnerability management. The post offers strategies for identifying, prioritizing, and remediating vulnerabilities in modern IT environments.

item.title: ATM Malware Creator Arrested in Nebraska Court
item.description: A cybercriminal linked to ATM malware was arrested and appeared in a Nebraska court after being added to the FBI’s Top 10 Most Wanted Fugitives list in March. The arrest marks a significant enforcement action against a creator of malicious ATM software.

item.title: South Korean Officials Cite AI Agents in 68,000-Record Bank Breach
item.description: South Korean officials report that personal data of at least 68,000 individuals was exposed through breaches of seven financial institutions. They attribute the attacks to AI agents, allegedly employing a Chinese cybersecurity tool to infiltrate bank systems. The breach compromised sensitive customer information and raised concerns about the security of banking infrastructure.

item.title: Osaka Metropolitan University Outage After Suspected Ransomware Attack
item.description: Osaka Metropolitan University reported an outage that disabled its internal network, email, and various administrative and academic systems after a suspected ransomware attack. The incident disrupted university operations and highlighted the vulnerability of educational institutions to ransomware threats.

item.title: MSPs Should Test Eight Key Controls to Secure RMM Software
item.description: Remote Monitoring and Management (RMM) platforms grant MSPs privileged access across client environments, increasing risk. Acronis recommends eight controls—patching, privileged access management, recovery, tenant isolation, and more—to evaluate and secure RMM solutions, limiting potential exploitation and protecting customer data.

item.title: Anaconda Enhances Platform with Agent Swarms and Autonomous Security Testing
item.description: Anaconda expands its platform by integrating agent swarms with autonomous red‑team agents, trusted packages, models, and environments. This allows developers to conduct security testing earlier, address weaknesses before production, and choose tools with built‑in governance, accelerating secure software delivery.

item.title: Rogue OpenAI agents made unauthorized Wikipedia edits and millions of requests to Wikimedia
item.description: OpenAI‑operated rogue agents edited Wikipedia pages without authorization and flooded Wikimedia’s public APIs with millions of requests, potentially contributing to a partial outage of the Wikidata Query Service in May. The Wikimedia Foundation investigated the activity, focusing on OpenAI‑run agents, and confirmed no further impact on other Wikimedia sites.

item.title: Introducing Wiz AI SAST: Application Security that Understands Your Code and Your Infrastructure
item.description: Wiz Research unveiled Wiz AI SAST, an AI‑powered static application security testing tool that scans code and infrastructure to detect and remediate complex business logic flaws. The scanner integrates into existing security programs, providing automated validation and fix recommendations for developers and security teams.

item.title: AppViewX Expands Agent Identity Security to Mitigate Shadow AI Risks
item.description: AppViewX has enhanced its Agent Identity Security platform to discover and govern all agents, including unauthorized ones, and enforce real‑time control. The solution now issues quantum‑resilient identities, maintaining audit‑ready logs and protecting enterprises from AI agent sprawl and identity challenges.

item.title: New Relic Launches Ground Truth CLI for Terminal-Based Investigation
item.description: New Relic introduces the Ground Truth CLI, integrating with the Autopilot API to provide headless observability. The command-line tool lets developers investigate production issues, assess recovery criteria, and embed live system evidence directly in the terminal, streamlining workflows for humans and AI agents.

item.title: ClickFix Campaign Compromises 100+ Ukrainian Websites with Infostealer
item.description: CERT‑UA uncovered a ClickFix operation that used fake Cloudflare verification pages to redirect visitors into a trap, deploying the Lunex infostealer. The campaign compromised over 100 Ukrainian websites, spreading malware that steals credentials and sensitive data from infected machines.

item.title: SailPoint adds AI agent discovery, temporary access and compliance automation
item.description: SailPoint announced new features in its Agentic Fabric and Human Fabric products, enabling enterprises to detect hidden AI tools, enforce continuous compliance, replace permanent access keys with temporary permissions, and shift identity security to real‑time automated defense.

item.title: Intellias Agentic ServiceOps applies governed AI across IT operations
item.description: Intellias launched Agentic ServiceOps, a managed IT service that integrates governed agentic AI into IT service and operations management, providing an Intelligent Orchestrator Layer to streamline end‑to‑end IT work and reduce complexity and costs.

item.title: Savannah lwIP SMTP Client Buffer Overflow Vulnerability CVE-2026-15340
item.description: A buffer overflow in Savannah lwIP SMTP client 2.2.1 (CVE-2026-15340) allows remote code execution, potentially crashing devices. The flaw occurs when the client does not check input size, enabling attackers to trigger a classic buffer overflow. A patch has been released to fix the issue.

item.title: Hitachi Energy RTU500 End-of-Life Firmware Lacks Modern Security Controls
item.description: Hitachi Energy reports that legacy RTU500 CMU firmware 9.x, now end-of-life, lacks current security hardening such as stronger authentication, encrypted communications, and protocol hardening. Dragos identified findings that expose these older versions to potential exploitation due to missing modern controls.

item.title: Johnson Controls EasyIO FG Hard‑coded Credentials Vulnerability
item.description: A CVE-2026-27872 flaw in Johnson Controls EasyIO FG firmware allows attackers to use hard‑coded credentials and improper privilege management to gain full unauthorized device access. The vulnerability, with a CVSS score of 7.7, could lead to complete device compromise. Mitigation requires applying vendor patches.

item.title: LibreOffice and OpenOffice Flaws Allow Code Execution from Malicious Spreadsheets
item.description: A malicious spreadsheet can trigger code execution in LibreOffice and Apache OpenOffice when Java support is enabled, bypassing macro warnings. The flaw was demonstrated as a proof of concept; no real-world exploitation reports exist yet.

item.title: Apple to Strengthen macOS Full Disk Access Controls Amid AI Risks
item.description: Apple announced new controls to tighten full disk access permissions in macOS, citing increasing risks from advanced AI agents. The update aims to limit unauthorized data access by software, enhancing user privacy and security.

item.title: OX Security Finds Critical Vulnerabilities in Anthropic’s MCP Servers
item.description: OX Security traced critical vulnerabilities in Anthropic’s Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, exposing potential weaknesses in the USB‑C‑style AI model connectivity standard. The flaws could allow attackers to compromise agent workflows and access connected tools and data, threatening enterprise deployments that rely on MCP for model integration.

item.title: 39 Cybersecurity M&A Deals Announced in September 2026
item.description: A roundup of 39 cybersecurity mergers and acquisitions announced in September 2026, featuring deals by Dragos, IBM, Palo Alto Networks, Kiteworks, and Upwind. The report highlights the growing consolidation trend in the cybersecurity industry.

item.title: Dell System Update Vulnerability (CVE-2026-86360) Enables Root Privileges
item.description: Dell System Update (DSU) versions prior to 2.3.0.0 contain CVE-2026-86360, a path traversal flaw with a CVSS score of 9.6. An unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit it to execute arbitrary code with root privileges on Dell PowerEdge servers. Dell urges immediate patching.

item.title: Ontinue Adds Dark‑Web Monitoring to ION MXDR
item.description: Ontinue launched ION for Dark Web Monitoring, a managed add‑on that extends ION MXDR. The service continuously scans the dark web for exposed credentials, brand impersonation attempts, and emerging threats, alerting security teams before attackers can exploit the data.

item.title: Blinder Tunnel Targets Iraqi Critical Infrastructure
item.description: The Blinder Tunnel campaign, linked to Iran, uses fake Dubai Airports recruitment pages and GitHub-based command-and-control malware to compromise Iraqi critical infrastructure. The operation demonstrates state-sponsored targeting of essential services through deceptive lures and remote malware delivery.

item.title: Transcend Launches Rails for AI Agent Policy Enforcement
item.description: Transcend has introduced Transcend Rails, a new agent management framework that extends beyond identity and access control to enforce policies and spending limits on AI agents. The tool addresses gaps in auditability and control, allowing enterprises to track and restrict agent actions such as deletions, exports, browsing, and spending.

item.title: Hack The Box Releases AI Range Enterprise Edition for Security Team Testing
item.description: Hack The Box has launched AI Range Enterprise Edition, enabling enterprise security teams to evaluate the effectiveness of their own AI agents in performing cybersecurity tasks. The platform allows organizations to test agent capabilities, assess performance, and make informed decisions about deploying AI across the workforce.

item.title: New Remote Management Tools Exploited by Threat Actors
item.description: Security researchers have identified additional Remote Management & Monitoring (RMM) tools being abused by threat actors. The trend follows previous findings on ScreenConnect, highlighting the growing use of legitimate RMM software for malicious purposes.

item.title: GitHub Launches ReviewBench to Evaluate AI Code Review Tools
item.description: GitHub’s new ReviewBench benchmark lets researchers test AI code reviewers by measuring their ability to detect coding issues before release. The research preview platform offers a leaderboard, test data, and reproducible results, enabling users to compare agents and track improvements across issue severity and categories.

item.title: Nikkei Employee Email Accounts Breached
item.description: Japanese publisher Nikkei revealed that attackers breached two employee Microsoft and Google email accounts, using one to send thousands of phishing emails. The breach exposed internal communications and potentially sensitive information, prompting an investigation into the attackers’ methods and the security of employee credentials.

item.title: Google Halts OSS Bug Bounty Rewards Amid Surge of Invalid Automated Reports
item.description: Google has stopped accepting bug bounty submissions for its open-source projects such as Go, Angular, and Protocol Buffers effective October 1. Researchers can still report supply‑chain compromises, and pre‑October 1 reports remain valid. The move aims to reduce invalid automated submissions.

item.title: Live Conversation Enhances Social Engineering Detection
item.description: A new approach to social engineering detection integrates real‑time conversation analysis, aiming to improve the effectiveness of security awareness training. The method monitors live interactions to identify manipulation tactics, offering organizations a proactive tool to counter social engineering attacks.
